newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Earthquake shakes Cyprus, felt as far as Israel.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake shakes Cyprus, felt as far as Israel.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.8 on the Richter scale hit the eastern Mediterranean island of Cyprus at noon on Monday, shaking tall buildings, geologists said.
There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage in the quake, which was felt as far away as the Israeli coastal city of Tel Aviv.
"The earthquake measured 5.8 on the Richter scale with an epicentre of 50 kilometres south west of Paphos," a Geological Service Department official told Reuters.
The Israel Seismology institute reported the quake measured 6.3 on the Richter scale. It was felt at 12.19 (1019 GMT) and lasted around 30 seconds in Cyprus.

Geologists described the tremor as an aftershock of a more powerful one measuring 6.5 on the Richter scale which struck on October 9 off the western coastal resort of Paphos. Aftershocks have been felt frequently since then.
"It is in the same seismological region. It was a big one (tremor) but it was an aftershock," the official added.
Cyprus radio correspondents said the tremor was strongest in Limassol and Paphos and felt to a lesser extent in the capital Nicosia.
